{{update|date=August 2025}}

'''Colin Skinner''' (born 1965) is a British author, adventurer and [[molecular biology|molecular biologist]] who is attempting to walk around the world.  As of mid-2014, he has walked over {{convert|14500|mi|km}} and has crossed [[Great Britain]], [[Iceland]], [[United States]] and [[New Zealand]].<ref name="Meet Doctor Colin Skinner">{{cite web|url=http://teacher.scholastic.com/zealand/meet.htm |title=Meet Doctor Colin Skinner |publisher=Teacher.scholastic.com |accessdate=2014-07-30}}</ref> He has used the walks to raise money and awareness for various causes, including [[conservation biology]], people with [[disabilities]], cancer relief, [[AIDS]], and [[hospice]].

==Education==
Skinner earned his [[Bachelor of Science]] (BSc) combined honours degree in [[biochemistry]] and [[genetics]] from the [[University of Leeds]].  He earned his [[PhD]] in [[molecular biology]] from [[University College London]].  He earned his [[Postgraduate Certificate in Education]] (PGCE) in secondary science from [[Canterbury Christ Church University]].

==Walking around the world==

===Scotland to England in 1984===
He began at the age of 18 at [[John o' Groats]] (at the northern tip of [[Scotland]]) in 1984, and walked to [[Land's End]] in [[England]].  On this journey, which he carried out with three other people, he pushed a wheelchair {{convert|1000|mi|km}} and raised £3,500 for The Forelands School for handicapped children.  In 1983, he had already run {{convert|21|mi|km}} around a 400-metre track to raise further money for The Forelands School for handicapped children, at [[Broadstairs]] in [[Kent]].

===Iceland in 1986===
In 1986, at the age of 20, whilst at the University of Leeds, he crossed [[Iceland]], together with three other students (Andrew Backhouse, David Brock and Shaun Fagan), from [[Seyðisfjörður]] in the east, through the interior to the north of the [[Vatnajökull]] ice fields, and then west to [[Reykjavík]].  The team encountered an 'ash storm', where storm force winds had whipped up fine black [[volcanic ash]], and had to wear goggles and face masks to push on into the winds.  In the [[rain shadow]] of the [[Vatnajökull]], they ran out of water, then encountered a flash flood, as mud rushed down from the melting [[glaciers]]. They also had to survive on food contaminated with [[petrol]] that had leaked from their petrol stoves.  This journey of {{convert|400|mi|km}} raised £2,000 for the Royal Association for Disability and Rehabilitation.  As part of the training for the walk across Iceland he ran the Leeds Marathon, in a time of 3 hours and 41 minutes.

On the Icelandic trek, he came up with the idea of walking {{convert|6000|mi|km}}, across Britain and America to raise money for [[Macmillan Cancer Support]] in Britain and [[Hospice care|hospice]] in America and [[Canada]].

===Scotland to England in 1988===
On 1 May 1988, he set off again from [[John o' Groats]], this time walking through the [[West Highlands]], down the [[Pennine Way]] and then south to [[Land's End]]: a distance of {{convert|1100|mi|km}} in seven weeks.  As part of the training for this walk he ran the gruelling [[Snowdonia Marathon]], in a time of 4 hours and 40 minutes.  The walk through Scotland and England raised £2,000 for [[Macmillan Cancer Support]].<ref>''Taking a walk across America,'' [[East Kent Mercury and Dover Mercury|East Kent Mercury]], 7 July 1988</ref>

===Across the U.S.A. in 1988/1989===
[[Image:TETON7.JPG|thumb|left|Colin Skinner walking by the [[Teton Mountains]]]]

The journey across the [[United States]] began on 15 July 1988.  On the journey he slept in bushes beneath the [[World Trade Center (1973–2001)|World Trade Center]], camped outside [[Kennedy Airport]] in a tent, then headed west.  On [[Staten Island]] he collapsed from heat exhaustion at 105 degrees [[Fahrenheit]].  In [[Utah]] the temperatures went down to minus 30 [[Fahrenheit]].  Carrying a tent and a backpack, with no backup, he walked alone to [[Niagara Falls]], through [[Ontario]] in [[Canada]], to [[Detroit]], between the [[Great Lakes]], across the [[Great Plains]], through the [[Rocky Mountains|Rockies]] in winter, to [[Yellowstone National Park]], then south to the [[Grand Canyon]], on to [[Las Vegas, Nevada|Las Vegas]], through [[Death Valley]] and then snowshoed over the [[Sierra Nevada (U.S.)|Sierras]] to reach [[San Francisco]].  In Death Valley, down to his last $13, Skinner found $200 in the desert, and he had $1 left when he crossed the [[Sierra Nevada (U.S.)|Sierras]] to reach [[Yosemite]] Valley.  The total distance he walked from [[New York City]] to [[San Francisco]], was {{convert|4952|mi|km}}.<ref>''Scotland to S.F. 6,000-Mile Hike for Hospices'' San Francisco Chronicle, 22 March 1989</ref>

On the journey he visited 70 hospices and appeared on television, radio and in newspapers to encourage support for hospices across the U.S. and Canada.  The mayor of San Francisco, [[Art Agnos]], proclaimed 21 March 1989, "Colin Skinner Day," in recognition of the attention he brought to the work of hospices with [[AIDS]] patients in the city.

Returning to [[United Kingdom|Britain]] after this walk, he obtained a job as a research assistant in Chemical [[Pathology]] at the [[Middlesex Hospital]] and went on to obtain a [[PhD]] in [[Molecular Biology]] at [[University College London]].  In 1992, whilst studying for his PhD, he also ran the [[London Marathon]], in a time of 4 hours and 41 minutes, to raise money to buy a computer for a young boy with physical disabilities.  Skinner's PhD involved developing genetic tests to detect [[congenital adrenal hyperplasia]] in children.<ref>Rumsby, G., Skinner, C., Lee, H.A. & Honour, J.W. (1992).  Combined 17α-hydroxylase/ 17,20 lyase deficiency caused by heterozygous stop codons in the cytochrome P450 17α-hydroxylase gene.  ''Clin. Endocrinol.'' '''39''':483–485.</ref> He had work published in a number of scientific journals.<ref>Rumsby, G., Skinner, C. and Honour, J.W. (1992). Genetic analysis of the steroid 21-hydroxylase gene following ''in vitro'' amplification of genomic DNA.  ''J. Steroid. Biochem.'' '''41''':827–829.</ref> In 1994 he had his work published in ''Human Molecular Genetics''.<ref>Skinner, C.A. & Rumsby, G. (1994). Steroid 11β-hydroxylase deficiency caused by a five base pair duplication in the ''CYP11B1'' gene.  ''Hum. Mol. Genet.'' '''3''':377–378.</ref>

In 1994, Skinner married Dr. Monica Schneider (also a molecular biologist), and in 1996 their son James was born.  From 1994 to 1996 Skinner worked as a Post-Doctoral Research Fellow at [[Vanderbilt University Medical Center]], in [[Nashville, Tennessee]].<ref>Keeney D.S., Skinner C., Travers J.B., Capdevila J.H., Nanney L.B., King L.E. Jr., Waterman M.R.(1998).  Differentiating keratinocytes express a novel cytochrome P450 enzyme, CYP2B19, having arachidonate monooxygenase activity.  ''J. Biol. Chem.'' 273 '''48''':32071-32079.</ref> The work he carried out there involved [[DNA sequencing|gene sequencing]] and [[protein purification]] of [[cytochrome P450]] enzymes.  His work was published in the ''Journal of Biological Chemistry''.<ref>Keeney D.S., Skinner C., Wei S., Friedberg T., Waterman M.R. (1998). A keratinocyte-specific epoxygenase, CYP2B12, metabolizes [[arachidonic acid]] with unusual selectivity producing a single major epoxyeicosatrienoic acid.  ''J. Biol. Chem.'' 273 '''15''':9279–9284</ref> From 1996 to 1997 Skinner took care of his infant son, James, whilst his wife continued to work at [[Vanderbilt University Medical Center]].

===New Zealand in 1998===
In 1998 he walked from [[Cape Reinga]] in the North Island, to [[Bluff, New Zealand|Bluff]], at the southern tip of [[New Zealand]]; a distance of {{convert|1500|mi|km}}.  On the journey he walked through the active [[volcano]] at [[Whakaari/White Island|White Island]], experienced earthquakes up to 4.9 on the [[Richter Scale]], clambered over [[glaciers]], swam with [[pinniped|seals]] and reported on [[conservation biology]] projects involving [[endangered species]].  Information from the journey was posted on the [[Internet]] for schoolchildren in the U.S. via the [[Scholastic Corporation]] Scholastic Network.<ref name="Meet Doctor Colin Skinner"/> In December 2010 Skinner completed a book about the journey and [[conservation biology]], ''New Zealand – 1500 miles on foot through – The Land of the Long White Cloud'' on an [[Internet]] website.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wattpad.com/story/2098040-new-zealand |title=New Zealand 1500 miles on foot through The Land Of The Long White Cloud |publisher=Wattpad |date=2012-09-09 |accessdate=2014-07-30}}</ref>

In 1999 he obtained a [[Postgraduate Certificate in Education|PGCE]] (Postgraduate Certificate in Education) from [[Canterbury Christ Church University]] in [[Canterbury]], England.  In 2000 he worked as a secondary school science teacher at St. Edmund's School in [[Dover]], teaching 11 to 16-year-olds.<ref>''What is it about teaching that's enticing so many of us Back to School?''  The Sunday Express Magazine, 7 November 1999</ref>

In 2001 he worked as a volunteer at a wildlife park, working on enrichment activities for animals.  From 2001 until 2003 he worked part-time at a [[post office]]. During this time, he also taught science to primary school children, in a 'Link-Scientist' scheme run by the pharmaceutical company [[Pfizer]], and took care of his son.

In 2003 his mother died from [[pancreatic cancer]], at the age of 59.  This prompted him to write the story of the {{convert|6000|mi|km}} journey across [[Great Britain|Britain]] and America.  In 2006 he finished the book ''Beyond the Setting Sun'', with an introduction by [[Ranulph Fiennes]], the renowned polar explorer and adventurer.<ref>[http://www.freewebs.com/drskinnersite/ranulphfiennesview.htm Dr. Colin Skinner's Site | Walking 6000 miles for hospice<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> The book was written to raise money for hospices in Britain, [[Canada]] and America.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://wattpad.com/story/2094649-beyond-the-setting-sun |title=Beyond the Setting Sun |publisher=Wattpad |date=2012-09-09 |accessdate=2014-07-30}}</ref>

===Scotland to England in 2007===
On 29 April 2007, he began walking again at [[John o' Groats]] and arrived at [[Land's End]] on 8 June, having covered {{convert|900|mi|km}} in 6 weeks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thisiscornwall.co.uk/ |title=news, entertainment, jobs, homes and cars |publisher=this is cornwall |accessdate=2014-07-30}}</ref> On the walk in Britain he visited 20 hospices and raised £10,000 for hospice through sales of his ''Beyond the Setting Sun'' book.

===U.S.A. in 2009===
[[Image:Colin Skinner in 2009.jpg|thumb|left|Colin Skinner wearing a [[Balaclava (clothing)|balaclava]] during snow storm in [[North Dakota]]]]

Starting on 22 August 2009, he walked from [[Kennedy Airport]] in [[New York City]] to within 15 miles of [[Devils Lake, North Dakota|Devil's Lake, North Dakota]].  This was a distance of {{convert|2053|mi|km}} and Skinner stopped his journey on 3 December 2009, after three days with windchills down to −30 [[Fahrenheit]].  During the trip Skinner had to make incisions in his feet to relieve the pressure from [[blisters]], suffered [[food poisoning]], met up with a [[wolf]] in [[Upper Peninsula of Michigan|Upper Michigan]], had to face down two wild dogs, and had [[ski masks]] frozen to his beard in [[North Dakota]].  On the journey he appeared on television, radio and in newspaper articles.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mlive.com/news/bay-city/index.ssf/2009/10dr_colin_skinner_stops_at_bria.html |title=MLive.com |publisher=MLive.com |access-date=2014-07-30 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140808063001/http://www.mlive.com/news/bay-city/index.ssf/2009/10dr_colin_skinner_stops_at_bria.html |archive-date=8 August 2014}}</ref> He also wrote a daily blog for the National Hospice Foundation.<ref name="nationalhospicefoundation.org">{{cite web|url=http://www.nationalhospicefoundation.org/i4a/pages/index.cfm?pageID=368 |title=Colin Skinner Is Walking—and Blogging—from NYC to Minot, ND to Raise Awareness of Hospice |publisher=National Hospice Foundation |date=2009-08-21 |accessdate=2014-07-30}}</ref> He met [[hospice]] patients, including one woman with a terminal illness, who said that at times she could forget she was ill, thanks to the care she received in a [[hospice]] house in [[Buffalo, New York]].  He also met a man with [[lung cancer]] who could not sleep in hospitals, where there was always someone coming to check on him. In the [[hospice]] house in [[Windsor, Ontario]], the man had a peaceful room to himself, where he could finally get some rest.<ref name="nationalhospicefoundation.org"/>

===U.S. in 2011===
On 10 September 2011, Skinner set off from mile marker 283 on [[U.S. Route 2]], {{convert|15|mi|km}} before [[Devils Lake, North Dakota|Devil's Lake, North Dakota]], and walked {{convert|2576|mi|km}} to [[Tuolumne Meadows]] in [[Yosemite National Park]], California.  The walk took him through [[North Dakota]], [[Montana]], [[Idaho]], [[Utah]], [[Arizona]], [[Nevada]] and into [[California]].  Skinner snow-shoed over [[Tioga Pass]] and camped in a tent in the [[Sierra Nevada (U.S.)|Sierra Mountains]] for several nights,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://thesheetnews.com/archives/12352 |title=Archives &#124; The Sheet – Part 12352 |publisher=Thesheetnews.com |accessdate=2014-07-30}}</ref> but was forced to stop walking after suffering from [[frostbite]] in both feet.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://mammothtimes.com/content/walking-dying-hiker-stares-death-eye |title=Walking for the dying, hiker stares death in the eye |work=Mammoth Times|date=2012-02-03 |accessdate=2014-07-30}}</ref> On the journey he appeared on television, radio and in newspapers and encouraged support for [[hospices]] taking care of people with serious illnesses.<ref name="nationalhospicefoundation.org2011">{{cite web|url=http://www.nationalhospicefoundation.org/i4a/pages/index.cfm?pageID=604 |title=Walking Across North America for Hospice |publisher=National Hospice Foundation |accessdate=2014-07-30}}</ref> Skinner is now writing a book about this journey, entitled ''America- 12000 miles on foot, a wing and a prayer''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.clipsyndicate.com/video/play/3151738/helping_hospice_brown_mon_01_02_2012 |title=Clip Syndicate Video: HELPING HOSPICE &#124; Brown &#124; MON 01/02/2012 |publisher=Clipsyndicate.com |accessdate=2014-07-30}}</ref>

In September 2012, Skinner completed a short story, entitled ''Chenga'', and published this on an [[Internet]] website.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wattpad.com/story/2109001-chenga |title=Chenga |publisher=Wattpad |date=2012-09-09 |accessdate=2014-07-30}}</ref> In October 2012, Skinner completed the second part of a [[science-fiction]] [[fantasy]] [[trilogy]], entitled ''Djara'', and published this on an [[Internet]] website.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wattpad.com/story/2174701-djara |title=Djara |publisher=Wattpad |date=2012-09-09 |accessdate=2014-07-30}}</ref>

Skinner has now begun writing the third part of the [[science-fiction]] fantasy trilogy, entitled ''Tau''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wattpad.com/story/2175992-tau |title=Tau |publisher=Wattpad |date=2012-09-09 |accessdate=2014-07-30}}</ref> The ''Chenga'', ''Djara'', ''Tau'' [[trilogy]] includes the themes of [[time travel]], [[Parallel universe (fiction)|parallel universes]], [[vampires]], shapeshifters, [[angels]], [[demons]] and descendants of the fabled [[Giant|giants]] known as the [[Nephilim]].

In 2012 Skinner published four short poems: ''Gaia'', ''The Dreaming'', ''New Zealand Water Torture'' and ''Life Jim But Not As We Know It'' on an [[Internet]] website.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wattpad.com/7554587-gaia |title=Gaia |publisher=Wattpad |date=2012-09-26 |accessdate=2014-07-30}}</ref>

He is planning future walks through [[Australia]], [[Japan]], [[China]], [[Tibet]], [[Afghanistan]], [[Iran]], [[Iraq]], [[Israel]], [[Egypt]] and [[Europe]].{{citation needed|date=January 2017}}
